title: Surge attenuation policy engine for Dedicated fleets: multi-signal targeter and safety fences
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated capacity that focuses on surge attenuation: maintaining throughput guarantees while preventing unsafe growth in fleet size. The engine must synthesize multiple signals (throughput, per-GPU tokens/sec, p95 latency, GPU occupancy, edge-cache hit rate, and error rate) into a single scaling intent, apply slope and quantum limits, and enforce per-tenant and fleet-level safety fences. It must support a hybrid control mode (predictive + rule-based fallbacks) and integrate with the existing rollout & canary system in the Console.
background: Existing autoscalers at Redwood focus on percentile targets and headroom credits. Operations has observed oscillations during sudden tenant bursts that cause expensive, unnecessary scale-ups followed by rapid scale-downs (cost spikes and cold-start latency). Product requests throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers (SLA-backed committed throughput) without exposing them to unbounded fleet expansion. We need a policy engine that trades off latency SLOs, committed throughput, and cost via explicit safety limits.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New policy produces stable scaling decisions during synthetic burst tests for 90% of tenants (no >30% over-provision relative to steady-state peak). 2) No oscillation (no more than 2 scale events per 10 minutes) in canary runs. 3) SLA-attainment: p95 latency stays within target for committed-throughput tenants during 95% of the test duration. 4) Safety fences block any single-tenant request to grow fleet by >15% in a 10-minute window without manual approval. 5) Integrates with Console rollout and emits tracing and cost-impact metrics.
decisions:
- Use a hybrid algorithm: short-horizon predictive headroom estimator (lightweight time-series model) to suggest scale intent and a rule-based stabilizer to limit growth and enforce fences.
- Primary target metrics: throughput (requests/sec adjusted by token density) and p95 latency; secondary signals: GPU utilization and model cache hit rate.
- Safety fences: max-percent-growth per-tenant window, fleet-level reserved capacity (min committed nodes), and soft-credit ledger for burst credits that decay.
- Implement slope-limiting: max growth rate 12% per 5 minutes; faster growth allowed only when predictive confidence is high AND multiple signals agree.
- Rollback policy: automatic rollback to previous fleet size if error rate increases by >200bps or p95 latency degrades by >40% post-scale.
tradeoffs:
- Predictive models reduce costly pre-warm misses but add complexity and risk of model misforecast; mitigated with conservative confidence thresholds and rule-based fallback.
- Using token-density normalized throughput improves cost/accuracy for long-context workloads but requires per-request metadata (token-estimates) from the API which could add telemetry overhead.
- Strict safety fences reduce cost but may cause transient SLO misses during massive sustained demand; we provide an emergency override path for ops during verified incidents.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Product. Agreed signals and initial safety thresholds.
2026-03-11: Prototype predictive headroom estimator sketched (exponential smoothing + demand markup). Running simulated traces against synthetic tenant workloads.

2026-03-12: Integration spike completed to surface GPU occupancy and model cache hit metrics into the autoscaler telemetry path. Identified missing tag on model_variant metric; created follow-up ENG-773556.
2026-03-13: Rule-based stabilizer spec drafted. Decided on slope-limiting numeric defaults and emergency override UX sent to Console team for review.
2026-03-14: Begun implementation of policy composer (golang). Added unit tests for growth-fence enforcement and simulated canary harness for 50 tenants.
comments: Miguel Santos (SRE): 'We need to ensure the predictive estimator operates in O(1) per-tenant and does not add per-request latency. Consider batched evaluation every 10s.'
Rina Patel (Product): 'Committed throughput customers expect precise billing alignment — include telemetry outputs that can be fed into billing reconciler.'
Daniel Park (Runtime): 'GPU occupancy alone is noisy for multi-tenant servers; prefer moving-average over 30s and combine with cache-hit-rate to avoid false positives.'
implementation_notes:
- Policy composer implemented as a stateless decision function that consumes time-windowed aggregates.
- Metrics inputs: requests/sec, estimated_tokens/sec, p95_latency_ms, error_rate, gpu_util_30s, cache_hit_30s.
- Outputs: target_node_delta (can be fractional, rounded by allocator), rationale tags for Console, confidence score.
- Persist soft-credit ledger in existing tenant-state store with TTL and decay rules.
- Ensure backward compatibility with older autoscaler clients: if predictive module disabled via feature flag, fall back to pure rule-based behavior.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for fence enforcement and slope limiters. 2) Canary in dedicated-staging region with 20 tenants including 3 committed-throughput customers. 3) Synthetic fuzz: replay production traffic traces with injected 5x bursts for 30 minutes. 4) Observability: traceable decision logs, pre/post-scale SLI snapshots, and cost delta reporting. 5) Ops playbook for emergency override and rollback.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: predictive overfit causes unnecessary scale ups. Mitigation: low-confidence threshold and shadow mode for 2 weeks.
- Risk: telemetry lag leading to stale decisions. Mitigation: require at least two agreeing signals and use conservative growth when telemetry is stale.
- Risk: per-tenant single actor causes a fleet-level spike. Mitigation: per-tenant per-window growth caps and cross-tenant burst arbitration.
next_steps: 1) Complete policy composer code and open PR (target 2026-03-18). 2) Console: add rationale tags and canary controls (ENG-774000). 3) Schedule canary run and billing alignment review with Finance. 4) Post-canary: enable default soft-credit decay to 50% for first 48 hours in production.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on the safety fence math and rollback triggers. Pay attention to CPU/GPU overhead of the predictive estimator and ensure it meets resource limits. The feature should be gated behind a tenant flag until billing reconciliation is in place.
